  Regular Meeting

  McCurley, Senior Planner; Megan Wu, Associate Planner; Kassandra

E.  DISCUSSION ITEMS:

  AGENDA
  ITEM 3:  ZONING CODE UPDATE
  • This is the seventh presentation in a series of presentations on the
  Comprehensive Zoning Code Update project presented by Planning
  Division Staff.
  • Recommended Action: It is recommended that the Planning
  Commission receive and file this informational report and provide
  input to Staff as deemed appropriate.
  • Principal Planner Paul Lam provided the Staff presentation.
  • Commissioner Comments – Objective Design Standards:
  o The Commissioners inquired if there is an objective way to
  address scale and preservation of privacy, and specifically,
  address buildings disproportionate in scale to neighboring
  buildings and privacy impacts upon residential uses.
  o The Commissioners commented that the draft Zoning Code does
  not appear to include specific requirements for green space in

  2
  12/05/2022
   multi-family residential developments and inquired if
  requirements for green space will be incorporated.
o  The Commissioners asked if there is a requirement for setback
  areas to be landscaped and if so, whether this can count toward
  open space requirements. The Commissioners suggested
  requiring landscaping in the side and rear yards in addition to the
  front yard.
o  The Commissioners suggested incorporating an objective design
  standard to require shade and shadow studies. The Commissioners
  requested Staff craft a specific measurable threshold for the shade
  and shadow studies in order to ensure it is an objective standard
  that can be verified.
o  The Commissioners suggested creating an objective design
  standard requiring proposed projects to be consistent with
  adjacent properties as well as requiring projects to give
  consideration to the architectural style of structures being
  demolished as part of a project.
o  The Commissioners discussed how adoption of an Historic
  Preservation Ordinance could help ensure projects are designed
  within the context of their setting.
o  The Commissioners stated more clarification on objective design
  standards is necessary.
o  The Commissioners discussed how specific standards are
  necessary to define certain architectural styles and stated the
  process to establish these standards will be important when
  classifying architectural styles within neighborhoods.
o  The Commissioners urged consideration of how certain standards
  have worked in the past and how others may work in the future.
o  The Commissioners inquired about the extent to which SB 35 and
  SB 330 require specific design standards, and asked whether there
  are State requirements to adopt certain objective design standards
  or if the City has the exclusive discretion to choose its design
  standards.
o  The Commissioners requested clarification on if there are design
  elements the State has indicated cities are not allowed to consider
  and if there are specific design elements cities must consider.
o  The Commissioners discussed the State’s desire for the City to
  develop design standards and stated that the State does not
  regulate what those design standards are, so long as they are
  objective and measurable.
o  The Commissioners explained that development standards can be
  so burdensome that it becomes hard to develop properties at their
  maximum density which constitutes a governmental constraint,
  and by utilizing objective design standards the City can create
  balance with standards that do not create a governmental
  constraint.
o  The Commissioners inquired into the role of the Design Review

  3
  12/05/2022
   Board with the implementation of new objective design standards.
  o The Commissioners asked if there can be exceptions to objective
  design standards, such as obtaining a Variance, and if so, what the
  process would be to make an exception to the standards.
•  Commissioner Comments – Sign Standards:
  o The Commissioners asked if the Supreme Court rulings
  referenced in the presentation on the proposed changes to sign
  standards were related to billboards.
  o The Commissioners asked if it is possible to amortize or phase out
  billboards within the City, noting that billboards can become
  nuisances with their lighting.
  o The Commissioners asked for clarification on the formula for
  calculating sign area and inquired if the changes were a result of
  business owners’ desire for larger signs, or if the change is a Staff
  effort to simplify and standardize the sign area formula.
  o The Commissioners inquired if the new allowances for sign sizes
  are permissible by-right or if there is any discretionary process for
  review of signs. The Commissioners further inquired as to what
  happens if a sign is too big.
  o The Commissioners asked why painted signs are prohibited, and
  then suggested an exception to the prohibition on painted signs be
  allowed for those signs which have historic qualities or are
  intended to convey a historic aesthetic. The Commissioners
  further recommended allowing art pieces that incorporate
  business names and advertisements within them, and asked
  whether there can be a specialized or discretionary process to
  address these types of signs.
•  Commissioner Comments – Nonconforming Uses, Buildings, and
  Lots:
  o The Commissioners inquired if there are other nonconforming
  features aside from setbacks that can be intensified or continued.
  o The Commissioners asked if there are limitations for properties
  with 0’ setbacks and how privacy can be protected in these
  instances, particularly when considering proximity of windows to
  neighboring properties.
  o The Commissioners suggested that the continuation of
  nonconformities should be required to meet certain minimum
  standards before allowing additions to be permitted by-right, and
  further expressed discomfort with allowing continuation or
  expansion of 0’ lot lines by-right. The Commissioners had
  additional discussion on whether to require a discretionary
  process or to allow a Staff-level review, and then recommended
  allowing the continuation of up to half of the required setback by-
  right, but requiring a discretionary review process for instances
  exceeding more than half of the required setback.
  o The Commissioners asked if property owners should attempt to
  achieve conformance with development standards when making
  4
  12/05/2022
   modifications to properties.
  o The Commissioners discussed examples of older properties with
  nonconforming features that are restricted in their ability to make
  modifications due to these nonconformities, and the need to have
  some leniency and balance of restrictions for these types of
  situations, especially when taking into consideration that there are
  Building Code and Fire Code requirements that will also impose
  certain limitations. The Commissioners further commented that
  the proposed flexibility within the Zoning Code will allow
  property owners to avoid a lengthy approval process to construct
  additions as well as the opportunity to construct additions without
  bringing existing structures into conformance. The
  Commissioners indicated that extreme measures and review
  should only be required for extreme instances.
  o The Commissioners indicated that by allowing half of the required
  setback to be continued, this would allow for some older
  structures to continue their setbacks.
  o The Commissioners inquired if there are other impacts to consider
  with continuation of nonconforming features, aside from privacy
  and impacts to neighbors.
  o The Commissioners asked if the intent behind the proposed
  changes is to ease Staff’s workload and to streamline the process
  for property owners, or if this was a result of new State
  requirements.
  o The Commissioners indicated that the proposed standard of
  allowing continuation of a setback that is at least half of the
  required setback should also be applied to nonresidential
  structures located adjacent to residential structures.
  o The Commissioners inquired if the nonconforming standards
  would be applicable to residential units in nonresidential zones,
  such as the block of residential uses in the Industrial zone along
  Lemon Street.
  o The Commissioners asked about situations when there are
  nonconforming commercial uses in residential areas that have
  been vacant for an extended period of time, and whether the
  Zoning Code would allow for these nonconforming commercial
  uses to be maintained as nonconforming uses rather than being
  required to convert to a residential use. The Commissioners
  expressed that maintaining such nonconforming commercial uses
  in residential areas provides amenities that contribute to
  walkability in neighborhoods, and stated the importance of
  preserving these uses.
•  Commissioner Comments – General Discussion:
  o The Commissioners stated that the issue of the boundaries for
  various zones, specifically along Main Street, including the CBD,
  EMC, and the DRD, continues to be raised, and inquired if the
  update to the Zoning Code will consider changes to these

  5
  12/05/2022
   boundaries. The Commissioners further stated that the issue of
  these boundaries should be revisited as part of the wrap-up
  process for the update to the Zoning Code to determine if there is
  consensus on this issue.
o  The Commissioners discussed the format for the final
  presentations and meetings leading up to adoption of the
  comprehensive update to the Zoning Code. The Commissioners
  inquired if there will be opportunity to discuss the draft and
  deliberate the proposed changes to achieve consensus, and then
  asked if one public hearing is sufficient time to allow for this
  discussion and deliberation. The Commissioners suggested more
  than one meeting before the public hearing will need to be
  scheduled for the Planning Commission, since further in-depth
  discussion is needed to obtain consensus on some areas of
  ambiguity.
o  The Commissioners asked for clarification on the meaning of one
  meeting and whether a single meeting can be continued to span
  several evenings until consensus on a recommendation can be
  achieved, especially when meetings concern complex issues.
o  The Commissioners discussed the format for the wrap-up
  presentation and inquired if the comment list provided on the
  Code Alhambra website will serve as a guide for discussion
  during the wrap-up meeting. The Commissioners also asked if an
  updated redlined version of the draft document would be provided
  for either the wrap-up presentation or the public hearing. The
  Commissioners stated the redlined version would be helpful for
  comparing the original draft with the revised draft, and
  understanding how the comments received to date have been
  reflected in the revisions. The Commissioners expressed their
  desire to receive a redlined version of the Zoning Code
  documents.
o  The Commissioners stated there are various components of the
  draft Zoning Code where it is unclear if there is consensus
  amongst the Commission, and suggested it may be useful during
  the wrap-up meeting to discuss those specific issues where a
  consensus has not yet been established.
o  The Commissioners asked for a timeframe for the City’s review
  of the Inclusionary Housing Ordinance, noting the importance of
  affordable housing.
o  The Commissioners expressed thanks to all those involved in the
  process to update the Zoning Code and expressed their desire to
  achieve consensus at the wrap-up meeting on where and how new
  housing units can be built within the City.
o  The Commissioners stated it would also be helpful to have Staff
  outline how the update to the Zoning Code fits with the Housing
  Element and specifically, the programs and policies that need to
  be implemented as part of the Housing Element in order to comply

  6
  12/05/2022
   with the City’s RHNA allocation.
  o The Commissioners indicated a preference to review the final
  language of the updated Zoning Code as one consolidated
  document in order to assess if the final edited language aligns with
  the Commission’s understanding of what was agreed upon and
  what was recommended. The Commissioners expressed a desire
  to have an opportunity in the adoption process to allow the
  Commission to verify there is no ambiguity in the language of the
  Zoning Code prior to adoption by the City Council.
  o The Commissioners inquired if they would have an opportunity to
  review the final language of the Zoning Code prior to it being sent
  to the City Council, and stated they want to receive the final
  version of the Zoning Code document prior to making any
  recommendations to City Council.
  o The Commissioners suggested having a future informational
  discussion item at a Planning Commission meeting where Staff
  can report back on any changes the City Council ultimately makes
  to the final Zoning Code document.
•  Public Comments:
  Burt Ng asked if the objective design standards presented will only
  be applicable to multi-family and mixed-use developments, or if it
  will also apply to single-family residential developments. Mr. Ng
  inquired if uses that were legally established are permitted to maintain
  and continue structures at their current setbacks, but that continuation
  of structures would not be allowed if the construction was originally
  done illegally without permits.
  Jennifer Ng commented that the continuation of nonconforming
  setbacks often arises in situations where properties have a setback of
  only 3’ or 4’. Ms. Ng suggested that the continuation of
  nonconforming setbacks be allowed if it is at least 3’ or 4’ as opposed
  to half of the required setback, and stated that there should be
  minimums to allow the City to have more control. Ms. Ng stated the
  continuation of a 0’ lot line would be too much. Ms. Ng thanked Staff
  for their work throughout the process to update the Zoning Code and
  asked if there would be an additional meeting after the wrap-up
  presentation to allow the Commission to respond to public comments
  received during the wrap-up meeting, prior to moving forward with
  final recommendations to the City Council at a public hearing. Ms.
  Ng also stated that over the past several years the City has increased
  efforts to have public participation and as a result she feels more heard
  by the City.
  Lewis McCammon expressed appreciation for the process to update
  the Zoning Code and suggested Staff include in the next agenda
  packet a table showing the changes originally proposed in the draft
  document alongside the changes that will be made to the document as
  a result of the comments received up to this point. Mr. McCammon
  noted the monumental effort required to comprehensively update the

  7
  12/05/2022
   Zoning Code and applauded Staff for their work on this project. Mr.
  McCammon expressed that the Commission will need as much
  information as possible on the changes that are being proposed and
  how these substantive changes are reflected in the Zoning Code
  document. Mr. McCammon also stated that prior to the public hearing
  with the Planning Commission it will be important to have the full
  document available to the public more than just 48 hours or 72 hours
  in advance of the meeting. Mr. McCammon further stated that there
  are still questions, including on the boundary between the Central
  Business District and the East Main Commercial corridor, and asked
  if there was a way to include this as part of the discussion at the
  December 19th Planning Commission meeting.

  MOTION:
  •  Moved to receive and file the informational report.
  •  Moved by Commissioner Sahu, Seconded by Commissioner Olson.
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote: 7-0
  Ayes:  Ho, Juarez, Olson, Sahu, Wang, Garcia, Gardea
  Noes:  None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: Mojarro, Pham, Tsujii
